name: Tank Volume Calculator
description: Calculate the volume of a cylindrical tank from diameter and height.

seo.title: Tank Volume Calculator: Cylinder, Rectangular & Spherical (Liters, m³)
seo.description: Calculate tank volume — Cylindrical, rectangular & spherical vessels with multiple unit options

formula.explanation: Cylinder volume V = πr²h where r = diameter/2. d and h in meters. ×1000 converts m³ to liters.

content.introduction: Calculate the volume of a vertical or horizontal cylindrical tank. This is used for storage tank sizing, capacity planning, and inventory calculations.

example.description: A 3m diameter × 6m tall cylindrical tank holds approximately 42,412 liters (42.4 m³).

faq.a: No, this calculates straight cylinder volume only. For dished ends, add approximately 10-15% additional volume depending on head type.

faq.q: How do I calculate horizontal tank partial volume?
faq.a: Partial volume (with liquid level) requires the circular segment formula, which is a separate calculation.

faq.q: How do I convert tank volume between m³ and gallons?
faq.a: 1 m³ = 1000 L = 264.17 US gallons. For example, a 50 m³ tank holds 13,208 US gallons. Convert using these factors for fill and hydrotest planning.

faq.q: How do I calculate the volume of a rectangular tank?
faq.a: V = L x W x H. A 4m x 2m x 1.5m basin: 4 x 2 x 1.5 = 12 m3 = 12,000 L (3,170 US gal).

faq.q: How many gallons does a 3m x 6m cylindrical tank hold?
faq.a: A 3m diameter x 6m tall tank holds 42,412 L, which is 42.41 m3 = 11,204 US gallons (9,329 imperial gallons).

faq.q: How do I calculate the volume of a spherical tank?
faq.a: V = pi/6 x D^3. A 3m sphere: pi/6 x 27 = 14.14 m3 = 14,137 L (3,735 US gal). Spheres minimize surface area for a given volume but are the most expensive tank shape to fabricate.

sections.heading: Unit Conversion for Tank Volume
sections.body:
**Volume units**

- 1 m³ = 1000 L = 264.17 US gal = 219.97 imp gal
- 1 US gal = 3.785 L
- 1 bbl (oil) = 42 US gal = 0.159 m³

**Length units**

- 1 m = 3.28084 ft
- 1 inch = 25.4 mm

Tank volume V = π/4 × D² × L (cylindrical) requires consistent units. Convert diameter and length to the same unit before computing, then convert the result to the desired volume unit.

sections.heading: Tank Volume Formulas for Common Shapes
sections.body:
Three standard geometries cover most storage tanks:
Cylindrical (vertical or horizontal): V = pi/4 x D^2 x H, where D = diameter and H = height or length. A 3m x 6m cylinder holds 42.4 m3.
Rectangular: V = L x W x H. A 2m x 2m x 2m basin holds 8 m3 (8,000 L).
Spherical: V = pi/6 x D^3. A 3m sphere holds 14.14 m3 (14,137 L).
Convert volume to liters by multiplying m3 by 1000, and to US gallons by multiplying m3 by 264.17.

sections.heading: Worked Example: 3 m x 6 m Vertical Cylinder
sections.body: A vertical cylindrical tank with D = 3 m and H = 6 m: radius = 1.5 m, so V = pi x 1.5^2 x 6 = 42.41 m3 = 42,412 L, or about 11,204 US gallons. This matches the calculator result. For the same tank laid horizontally with a partial liquid level, use the circular segment method: find the segment area from the fill height, then multiply by the tank length - the filled volume is not a linear fraction of the total volume.
